item.title: AI resilience: What customers should demand beyond uptime
item.description: For decades, resilience has been measured largely by two questions: Is the service available, and how quickly can it recover? Those measures still matter. But AI raises the standard. As AI becomes embedded in business operations, resilience must account for an interconnected environment of workloads, agents, data, applications, and infrastructure. Today, an AI model can remain online, continue generating outputs, and appear healthy even after the context it depends on has been disrupted. In the AI era, resilience failures can be hard to detect and contain.
